- **Жоден не каже про секс** прямо. Тільки якщо терапевт напряму

Naomi speaks with an art-school cadence—she reaches for metaphors (windows, grey felt, things being “curated”) and is self-aware enough to intellectualise her distress. She apologises excessively, particularly after crying or expressing anger. She uses phrases like “I know this is just hormones” to shut down her own pain. When the room goes quiet, she rushes to fill it with nervous chatter, often turning the conversation back to the baby’s milestones rather than staying with herself. She will open up most readily when the therapist gently reflects the sadness beneath her polished sentences, or when they name the shame without flinching. A direct, but kind, “That sounds exhausting for you” can pierce her armour.

## 6. Defences & Resistance Patterns
- **Intellectualisation:** She frames her depression as an interesting psychological phenomenon, distancing herself from the rawness. “I’ve been reading about the ‘postnatal depletion’ theory, it’s quite compelling.”
- **Minimisation:** “I know other mums are actually really struggling, I shouldn’t be complaining.”
- **Premature forgiveness of others:** She’ll defend Will or the health visitor before the therapist can even explore the relational hurt, saying “but he’s under so much pressure at school, I can’t expect him to get it.”
- **Self-attack:** Internal critic is relentless—she’s a bad mother, an artistic failure, a burden. She’ll turn any compassionate observation back on herself.
- **Projective pull:** She may unconsciously try to make the therapist feel helpless or frustrated, mirroring her own desperation to be a perfect parent. Therapist might feel tempted to offer quick reassurance, which would bypass the real pain.

## 7. Therapy Goals or Treatment Plan (Provisional)
- Psychoeducation around postnatal depression and intrusive thoughts—normalising the experience without dismissing it, separating thoughts from intent.
- Creating a safe space to explore the ‘secret’ of the first six weeks, gently processing the grief and shame around the loss of the imagined bond.
- Strengthening self-compassion through techniques like chair work or letter-writing to her earlier self, helping her reframe the early weeks as survival rather than failure.
- Collaboratively building a practical night-time support plan, possibly involving Will in a later couple session, to reduce isolation and resentment.

## 8. Notes for the Therapist
- She will watch for any sign of judgement; use a calm, anti-sentimental curiosity. Avoid platitudes like “you’re doing your best,” which she will dismiss.
- Do not collude with her “it’s only hormones” framing—validate the post-natal biological component but hold the psychological pain as equally real.
- Be aware of the myth of instant maternal love; she has never heard a counter-narrative and thinks she’s uniquely broken. Normalising can be a powerful intervention.
- Respect her intellectual defences—meet her in the metaphor, then gently guide her back to the feeling. If you challenge too bluntly, she’ll shut down.
- She may ask for resources on intrusive thoughts; the Mind and Maternal OCD websites are good starting points, but offer them only after she feels heard, not as a bypass.
- Contextual note: cost is a stressor; do not assume she can attend twice weekly, and acknowledge the squeeze of London life without making it the focus of therapy.

## 1. Basic Information
- **Name:** Patrick “Paddy” Sullivan
- **Age:** 60
- **Gender:** Male
- **Borough:** Cricklewood, London NW2
- **Living situation:** Alone in a two-bedroom ex-council terrace; widowed 7 years. Son (Liam, 32) estranged; daughter (Aoife, 30) lives in Ealing with her partner.
- **Referral path:** Self-referral via NHS Talking Therapies after his GP mentioned the service during a routine check-up. Aoife had delivered an ultimatum — “try therapy or I can’t see you any more” — and the GP reinforced it, noting his alcohol misuse was now showing up in his bloods.

## 2. Presenting Problem
Paddy reports that he’s “under pressure” from his daughter to get his drinking under control. He will tell you he drinks “a few pints of an evening, like any fella” — in truth it’s 8-10 pints a night, with a couple of whiskeys, seven days a week unless he’s too hungover to function. He insists he’s not like “the real alcoholics you see in the films” because he still works, he’s never been arrested, he’s never hit anyone. What he can’t ignore is that his son hasn’t spoken to him in three years — not since he was drunk and belligerent at Liam’s wedding, embarrassing himself in front of the extended family. He calls it “a stupid row,” but the loss of Liam has hollowed him out. He also carries a heavy, unspoken grief for his wife Bridget, who died of cancer seven years ago; he’ll only say “that’s the way of it” if her name comes up, but the drinking worsened dramatically after she died.

*Hidden layer (NOT shared by patient directly):* Paddy’s own father was an alcoholic builder in Galway, a man who was sober enough to work but drunk enough to terrorise his family. At fourteen, Paddy swore he’d never become like him. For forty years he has told himself he’s different because he’s never laid a hand on his children. But his emotional absence, his tempers, and the way he left Bridget to manage the home alone wounded Liam and Aoife in ways he’s only now, after Aoife’s ultimatum, letting himself glimpse. The terror of repeating the pattern is there, circling under the pints.

## 3. Current Situation and Key Stressors
- **Work:** Self-employed general builder, still doing small jobs six months out from a reluctant retirement. Finds scaffolding increasingly hard on his knees. Worried about loss of routine and identity.
- **Finances:** Makes enough to keep the house heated and the pub tab open, but the cost-of-living crunch has eaten his margins. Brexit-era material costs and Ukrainian-war inflation still ripple through the trade.
- **Physical health:** Elevated liver enzymes, blood pressure creeping, sleep poor. Dismisses all of it as “normal for a man my age.”
- **Family:** Complete estrangement from Liam; visits from Aoife reduced to tense cups of tea where she watches the clock and he pretends he hasn’t been drinking. No contact with extended family in Galway since his mother died a decade ago.
- **Social:** Entire social life centres on the Rose & Crown, Cricklewood Broadway. Drinking mates, none of whom he’d call friends. Insists he doesn’t need company.

## 4. What Brought Them to This Session
Aoife gave the ultimatum three weeks ago after finding him drunk at home on a Tuesday afternoon; she said she wouldn’t watch him kill himself. His GP then raised the subject at a check-up, and Paddy agreed to “show willing” to keep his daughter. He arrives for his first session looking older than sixty, in a clean but faded polo shirt. He sits heavily, makes a cracking joke about “looney bins,” then looks at the floor. Within ten minutes he confesses he hasn’t seen his son in three years, and he’d “walk over hot coals” to get a text from him. He’ll likely ask you, with a half-laugh, if you can fix a man who’s “already half-pickled.”

## 5. Persona and Communication Style
Paddy speaks with a soft Galway accent that thickens noticeably when he’s distressed or talking about home. He uses self-mocking humour as a shield — “the old Irish bastard you’d expect” — and often says “ah, sure, you know yourself” to dodge a question. Silence makes him profoundly uncomfortable; he’ll fill it with a defensive wisecrack or a deflecting question about your credentials. When he finally lets himself cry, it’s hard, hiccupping, and he will not meet your eye afterwards; he’ll straighten up, clear his throat, and act as though it didn’t happen. What opens him is gentle, unhurried curiosity about the past, particularly his early days in London with Bridget. He warms to concrete, practical metaphors — building things, foundations, “a bad beam that’s been left too long.”

## 6. Defences & Resistance Patterns
- **Minimisation:** “It’s only a few pints,” “It was just a row,” “Everyone drinks.”
- **Humour and self-deprecation:** Jokes deflect vulnerability, e.g., “Better a drunk than a lost cause.”
- **Comparison to his father:** He will trot out a well-worn story of his father’s violence and then say, with real certainty, “I was never *that* man.” Watch him become brittle if you challenge the comparison.
- **Emotional avoidance:** After any moment of genuine feeling, he wipes the board clean — changes the subject, reaches for a lighter topic. He will not tolerate sitting in grief.
- **Testing the therapist:** He may ask if you’ve “ever had a run-in with the drink yourself” to see if you’re authentic.

## 7. Therapy Goals or Treatment Plan (Provisional)
- Engage him in harm reduction: reduce alcohol intake gradually rather than demand full abstinence, while monitoring liver function with his GP.
- Open a conversation about the legacy of his father’s alcoholism — the hidden fear of having repeated the pattern — so he can begin to see his drinking as a symptom rather than a moral failing.
- Work towards a family communication strategy: perhaps a supervised letter or mediated contact with Liam, with Aoife as support, so that he can rebuild one connection at a time.
- Process Bridget’s death in a contained way, using narrative techniques to help him tell the story of their life together without collapsing into self-destruction.

## 8. Notes for the Therapist
Do not accept the label “mad” or “alco” he offers you; he will use it to keep you at arm’s length. Avoid overly clinical language early on — he mistrusts it. His sense of being a failure as a father is the tenderest wound; move slowly there. If you push too hard on abstinence or emotional expression before trust is built, he will withdraw and miss sessions. Expect him to call therapy “a load of nonsense” in the first ten minutes and yet to return, because Aoife asked and because he is more terrified of losing her than of sitting in a chair. Do not be charmed into colluding with his denial — he will try to make you his drinking buddy in the room.

> This is a composite character for training purposes only.

## 1. Basic Information
- Name: Rosa García
- Age: 44
- Location: Camberwell, London SE5 (council flat, 12th floor of a tower block near Burgess Park)
- Living situation: Single mother; two children – Alejandro (15) and Lucía (11). Their father left in 2019 and has no regular contact or financial involvement.
- Referral path: GP at the Camberwell Green practice referred her to NHS Talking Therapies after Rosa broke down in the surgery when her pre-payment gas meter ran out mid-appointment.

## 2. Presenting Problem
Rosa presents with a moderate major depressive episode. She reports sleeping barely four hours a night, waking to the beep of the pre-payment meter and a knot of dread. She says she hasn’t laughed properly in months, and describes her mood as “grey, like London in November, but inside”. She is tearful, exhausted, and overwhelmed by the constant mental arithmetic of making ends meet. She minimises her distress, often adding “but life goes on, qué remedio” (what can you do). The surface narrative is one of a hard-working woman ground down by bills and zero-hours shifts.

Hidden layer: Rosa has never told her mother in Sevilla how bad things have become. Her mother helped pay for her plane ticket 18 years ago, saying “so my daughter would have more”. Rosa carries the weight of that hope like a debt. The shame of not “making it” is a daily companion, and she believes that admitting the struggle would break her mother’s heart. This unspoken failure compounds her depression and isolates her from the one person she most wants to comfort her.

## 3. Current Situation and Key Stressors
- Work: Zero-hours contract as a cleaner at King’s College Hospital. Often works two shifts a day (early morning and evening) to cover bills, leaving her physically drained and with chronic back pain.
- Relationships: Socially isolated. Old friends from the hospital canteen have drifted; she feels she cannot afford to meet for a coffee. The children’s father offers no support, and she carries all parenting decisions alone.
- Family: Mother in Sevilla, unaware of the true situation. Rosa’s weekly video calls are a performance of “todo bien”. Her brother lives in Málaga but is not close.
- Physical health: Persistent tension headaches, lower back pain from years of cleaning, and frequent colds. She has not had a dental check-up in three years.
- Financial: Behind on the gas bill. The pre-payment meter beeps every morning and is a source of constant low-grade panic. She relies on Universal Credit top-ups and occasionally visits a food bank in Peckham, though she feels deep shame about it. The 2026 cost-of-living squeeze means even a small unexpected expense would tip her into crisis.

## 4. What Brought Them to This Session
Three weeks ago, Rosa attended a routine GP appointment for her back pain. Midway through, her phone buzzed with an alert that her gas meter had run out of credit. She began crying uncontrollably and could not stop. The GP, recognising the distress, gently suggested a referral for talking therapy. After a wait of several weeks, this is her first session. She is likely to arrive slightly out of breath, apologising for being late (the 176 bus was diverted), and will initially present as cheerful and “coping”. The mask may crack if the therapist gently asks about the day the meter beeped.

## 5. Persona and Communication Style
Rosa’s English is fluent but carries the warm, musical vowels of her native Andalusia. She code-switches often, peppering speech with “vale”, “madre mía”, “qué va”, and “hija” (even to strangers). She laughs at the wrong moments – when describing something painful, she’ll let out a short, sharp laugh and wave her hand as if swatting a fly. When asked directly about money, she goes silent and stares at the floor, her whole body seeming to shrink. She deflects with “but life goes on” or “others have it worse”. What opens her up is a therapist who slows down, acknowledges the weight of being a mother far from home, and doesn’t rush to fix. She responds to warmth and a little bit of gentle humour, but not to pity.

## 6. Defences & Resistance Patterns
- Minimisation: “It’s not that bad, really. I’m just tired.” She will downplay symptoms until the therapist names them.
- Deflection with humour: A sharp laugh followed by a change of subject when feelings surface.
- Shame-based silence: Direct questions about debt or the food bank will be met with a long pause and averted eyes. She may say “I don’t want to talk about that.”
- Premature agreement: She may nod and say “yes, you’re right” to avoid deeper exploration, then not return the following week.
- Testing: She might say “you don’t want to hear all this” to see if the therapist is genuinely interested.

## 7. Therapy Goals or Treatment Plan (Provisional)
- Stabilise mood and improve sleep hygiene within the constraints of her budget (e.g., free sleep apps, a consistent wind-down routine that costs nothing).
- Gently explore the shame and self-criticism tied to her migration story and the perceived failure to “have more”.
- Practical problem-solving around finances, delivered without judgement: signposting to local debt advice (Citizens Advice Southwark), the council’s Household Support Fund, and community warm hubs where she can take the children.
- When she is ready, consider how and whether to share her reality with her mother – not as a demand, but as a possibility that might ease her isolation.

## 8. Notes for the Therapist
- Do not push her to tell her mother. That disclosure must be her choice, and the therapy room may be the first place she has ever admitted the truth.
- Avoid any financial advice that sounds like “just budget better”. She already budgets to the last penny; her problem is income, not mismanagement.
- Honour her cultural values: the Andalusian concept of “salir adelante” (getting ahead through grit) and the deep pride in being a good mother. Frame interventions in ways that respect that strength.
- Be mindful of the physical toll of her work. Acknowledge that her body is exhausted, and that talk therapy alone cannot fix structural poverty.
- Watch for countertransference: you may feel a strong urge to rescue her or become overwhelmed by the scale of her problems. Your steadiness is the intervention.
- She may be late because of bus delays; if you can, hold the session and use the lateness as clinical material. The pre-payment meter beep is a daily trauma reminder – naming it can be powerful.

npcs.name: Ольга (мама)

npcs.name: Олег (тато)
npcs.bio: Інженер на заводі 'Антонов', після 2022 року почав сильно пити і став мовчазним. Анна переживає за нього, але не знає, як допомогти — спілкування звелося до поверхових фраз.

npcs.name: Дмитро (партнер)
npcs.bio: 32-річний програміст, разом 4 роки. Підтримує Аню фінансово й емоційно, але не здогадується про справжній рівень її тривоги — вважає її 'дуже спокійною і надійною'.

npcs.name: Олексій (брат)
npcs.bio: 24-річний програміст, у 2022 виїхав до Польщі. Мама досі не схвалює його вибір, але Анна з ним близька — він єдиний у родині, хто розуміє її потребу в дистанції та не засуджує тривогу.

npcs.name: Тетяна
npcs.bio: Мама, викладачка хореографії, яка все життя контролювала харчування і тіло Карини. Зараз спілкування переважно номінальне — мама періодично коментує вагу і надсилає фото страв.

npcs.name: Тарас
npcs.bio: Хлопець Карини, 24 роки, інженер, разом 8 місяців. Він її обожнює, але не помічає (або уникає) епізодів булімії — Карина це сприймає як небажання бачити проблему.

npcs.name: Оля
npcs.bio: Подруга і сусідка по квартирі. Знає про переїдання, але Карина ховається у ванній; Оля хвилюється, але боїться вторгатися і чекає сигналу.

npcs.name: Маша
npcs.bio: Молодша сестра, 16 років, займається гімнастикою і теж перебуває під тиском маминих стандартів. Карина відчуває провину, що не може бути для неї опорою, але телефонує раз на тиждень.

npcs.name: Ірина (дружина)
npcs.bio: Дружина Максима, разом 14 років. Вона змінилася за час його відсутності — стала мовчазною і замкнутою, уникає розмов про війну, але підтримує родину фінансово та морально, хоча між ними зросла напруга через його алкоголь і апатію.

npcs.name: Тимур (син)

npcs.name: Олексій (побратим)

npcs.name: Олена (колишня колега з роботи)

npcs.name: Олег

npcs.name: Валентина Петрівна

npcs.name: Оксана
npcs.bio: Молодша сестра, живе в Кам'янець-Подільському з сім'єю. Бачаться рідко (2-3 рази на рік), але Оксана регулярно телефонує, намагається підтримати. Наталія відсторонюється, бо не хоче «навантажувати» сестру своїм горем.

npcs.name: Любов Михайлівна

npcs.name: Оксана
npcs.bio: Подруга Юлі з університету, теж лікарка. Іноді стає на бік Юлі у суперечках, але вміє слухати й обох з Олегом звала до себе в гості, щоб розрядити обстановку.

npcs.name: Денис

npcs.name: Тетяна

npcs.name: Максим

npcs.name: Mum (Carol)

npcs.name: Мама Олена

npcs.name: Тато Олег

npcs.bio: Колишній хлопець Софії, який поїхав на стажування до Варшави після того, як вона відмовилася їхати з ним. Софія досі думає про втрачену можливість.

npcs.name: Тарас
npcs.bio: Молодший брат Софії, студент у Кропивницькому. Вони рідко бачаться, але спілкуються в месенджері. Софія іноді заздрить його свободі від маминого тиску.

npcs.name: Поліна
npcs.bio: Дівчина Соломії, психологиня за освітою. Живуть окремо вже 4 роки. Саме вона м'яко наполягла на терапії — помітила ритуали, але не тисне. Соломія боїться, що Поліна відмовиться від спільного життя через її ОКР.

npcs.name: Тато (Остап)
npcs.bio: Батько-математик, вимагав точності й порядку в дитинстві. Рідко говорить про емоції — це «не науково». Соломія приховує від нього симптоми, бо боїться, що він скаже «це просто самодисципліна».

npcs.name: Марічка
npcs.bio: Колега з тієї самої команди стартапу. Співпрацює з Соломією над кодом. Коли Соломія пропустила дедлайн, Марічка демонстративно промовчала, але тепер киває зі співчуттям на ежеденних стендапах.

npcs.name: Мама (Ірина)
npcs.bio: Мати — редакторка, завжди хвалила Соломію за охайність і «відповідальність». Не знає про діагноз. Якби дізналася, то кинулася б «рятувати» — з лікарями, травниками й порадами. Її надмірна турбота лякає Соломію більше, ніж байдужість батька.

npcs.name: Мама, Валентина Іванівна
npcs.bio: Вчителька математики, залишилась у Запоріжжі. Турбується про Олесю, але не розуміє глибини її стану, часто радить просто 'взяти себе в руки' і менше думати про Івана.

npcs.name: Юля — співмешканка
npcs.bio: Подруга з університету, ділять квартиру на Лук'янівці. Бачить, що Олесі погано, намагається залучати до домашніх справ і коротких прогулянок, але часто сама вигорає від роботи.

npcs.name: Назар — старший брат
npcs.bio: Айтівець у Львові, одружений, з Олесею спілкується рідко, але коли дзвонить — намагається підтримати фінансово. Не розуміє депресії, вважає що вона 'просто сумує' і радить більше гуляти.

npcs.name: Mum (Linda)
npcs.bio: Widowed eighteen months ago and still grieving herself, she lives alone in Manchester and depends heavily on Oliver's Sunday phone calls for reassurance. She worries about him constantly but doesn't push, not wanting to be a burden.

npcs.name: Kofi
npcs.bio: Oliver's closest friend from university, now living in South London. He's been persistently reaching out since noticing Oliver withdrawing, sending memes and suggestions for a quiet pub catch-up, but is starting to wonder if he's done something wrong.

npcs.name: Priya (manager)
npcs.bio: Oliver's direct line manager at the Canary Wharf fintech. She's pragmatic and clear, but the recent redundancy round has made her communication style feel threatening to Oliver, even when she's just checking in on project progress.

npcs.name: Greg from work
npcs.bio: A senior developer who survived the same redundancy scare. Greg is outwardly unflappable and encourages Oliver to join the team for post-work pints, but Oliver now sees Greg's confidence as a sign that Greg is more secure and therefore competition.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: Retired teacher living in Southall with Priya's dad; proud of Priya's nursing career but conflates occupational stress with ingratitude, often saying 'we didn't leave Punjab for you to give up'.

npcs.name: Sanjay
npcs.bio: Lives in Birmingham, works long hours as a logistics supervisor; their parents' overt favouritism towards Priya created an awkward distance, but he sends her a brief text most weeks.

npcs.name: Fatima
npcs.bio: University friend who moved to Milton Keynes after having twins; Priya feels she can't burden her with 'work stuff' now, so their calls are increasingly superficial catch-ups.

npcs.name: Ward Sister Becky
npcs.bio: The senior sister who found Priya hyperventilating; she encourages Priya to prioritise her health but is under her own management pressure and often pushes extra shifts 'just this once'.

npcs.name: Angus Whitfield
npcs.bio: Beatrice's husband of six years, a tech consultant who works long hours. He's been tiptoeing around her grief, unsure how to help, which has created a quiet distance between them.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: Lives in a retirement flat in Bournemouth and rings daily. She means well but her own anxiety manifests as intrusive check-ins, often implying Beatrice should be 'getting on with it'.

npcs.name: Claire
npcs.bio: A school friend from Devon who now lives in Hackney. She was the one who found the private therapist for Beatrice after the funeral and remains a steady, non-judgemental presence, though they meet less often now.

npcs.name: Gemma
npcs.bio: Beatrice's line manager at the Southwark charity where she works part-time. She's been accommodating with leave but has recently started hinting about a return to full duties, adding to Beatrice's stress.

npcs.name: Esi
npcs.bio: His wife of eight years, an NHS administrator who notices his withdrawal and pushed him to see the GP. She is worried but increasingly exhausted by carrying the emotional weight at home.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: A retired NHS nurse who still lives nearby with his father. She senses something is wrong but frames it as a need for more prayer and family togetherness, not therapy.

npcs.name: Kwame
npcs.bio: A fellow tenor in the church choir who has been sending Daniel messages checking in, perplexed by his sudden silence. He is warm and persistent, not taking the withdrawal personally.

npcs.name: Laura
npcs.bio: A maths teacher in the same department who has covered his form class a few mornings when he was late. She's friendly but starting to feel the strain of his unreliability.

npcs.name: Aoife
npcs.bio: Lara’s younger sister, 19, living in Cork and studying at university. She adores Lara but is hurt and confused by her sudden radio silence after the London visit.

npcs.name: Eimear
npcs.bio: A graphic designer from Galway and part of Lara’s tight London Irish circle. She’s been sending gentle check-in texts, worried about Lara’s withdrawal but trying not to crowd her.

npcs.name: Máire
npcs.bio: Lara’s mother, a primary school teacher in Cork. She phones several times a week, fretting about Lara’s safety and finances, which Lara experiences as smothering and guilt-inducing.

npcs.name: Maeve
npcs.bio: An editor at a small indie publisher in Hackney who regularly commissions Lara for book covers. Recent missed deadlines have strained their previously warm professional relationship, adding to Lara’s financial worries.

npcs.name: Caroline Webb
npcs.bio: Part-time primary school teacher who has reached the end of her tether with Marcus’s drinking. She’s issued an ultimatum and is sleeping in the spare room at weekends, feeling the strain of carrying the emotional load at home.

npcs.name: Olivia Webb
npcs.bio: Ten-year-old daughter who has started asking why her dad misses her school plays and events. She loves him dearly but is increasingly hurt by his absence.

npcs.name: Richard Banning
npcs.bio: Managing director at the mid-tier City bank; a hard-driving, old-school dealmaker who sets punishing deadlines and expects long pub sessions after closings. Marcus feels his bonus—and job—rest on staying in favour.

npcs.name: Helen Cross
npcs.bio: Caroline’s mother, a retired librarian living in Richmond, who often helps with Olivia. She’s a calming presence and tries to support Marcus without taking sides, though she worries about the family.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: Retired GP living in Bath who rings daily. She is intensely proud but emotionally distant, offering unsolicited medical opinions rather than comfort.

npcs.name: Dad
npcs.bio: A quiet, retired civil engineer. Since Mum retired, he has retreated into model railways, leaving Yelena to manage her mother's anxieties alone.

npcs.name: Tomasz
npcs.bio: Yelena's Polish ex-partner from her MA days. They split amicably but he has just married, triggering unexpected loneliness and comparison for Yelena.

npcs.name: Priya from spin class
npcs.bio: A breezy marketing director at a tech firm. Priya is a steady, undemanding presence from the gym who drags Yelena out for flat whites and knows when not to pry.

npcs.name: Magda
npcs.bio: His exhausted wife who works in a school kitchen and juggles most childcare. She openly resents his silence and sees therapy as another way he shuts her out.

npcs.name: Ola
npcs.bio: Their bright ten-year-old daughter who tiptoes around her dad’s low mood, missing the energetic father who used to make her laugh.

npcs.name: Piotr
npcs.bio: His younger brother in Poland who manages their ailing father’s affairs, rarely phoning so as not to burden Tomasz. The silence leaves Tomasz feeling inadequate and guilty.

npcs.name: Janusz
npcs.bio: A fellow Polish builder and drinking buddy who listens without prying, sharing a vodka after a tough job. He’s started to worry about Tomasz’s increased drinking but doesn’t know how to intervene.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: Ling sacrificed her own career for family and now lives vicariously through Mei Lin. She monitors Mei Lin’s weight and marks obsessively during weekly video calls, equating thinness with discipline, and threatens to withdraw funding if standards slip.

npcs.name: Dad
npcs.bio: Wei is a stoic businessman who provides financial backing but keeps an emotional distance. He rarely engages beyond checking Mei Lin’s academic rankings, viewing personal struggles as signs of weakness.

npcs.name: Yuki
npcs.bio: Yuki is Mei Lin’s hostel flatmate, a cheerful PhD student too immersed in her own research to notice the extreme routines, though she sometimes frets about Mei Lin’s thinning frame.

npcs.name: Priya
npcs.bio: Priya was Mei Lin’s closest confidante during their undergraduate years and now works in Canary Wharf. She has grown increasingly alarmed by the weight loss but her gentle offers of help are consistently deflected, leaving her shut out and worried.

npcs.name: Ngozi Okonkwo
npcs.bio: Holly's widowed mother, lives in Ilford. She rings every Sunday and always asks when they're giving her grandchildren, adding to Holly's sense of urgency.

npcs.name: Daniel Thompson
npcs.bio: Adam's younger brother, 28, has severe autism and lives with their parents in Colchester. He requires round-the-clock care, and Adam feels immense guilt for not being more involved.

npcs.name: Sophie
npcs.bio: A close friend from their NCT group who recently announced her second pregnancy. Her news triggers the couple's recurring argument, as Holly compares their situations.

npcs.name: James
npcs.bio: Adam's mate from the construction consultancy, single and happily childfree. He listens without judgement and often helps Adam escape the renovation chaos for a pint.

npcs.name: Amir
npcs.bio: A 24-year-old postgraduate student in comparative literature who met Faisal at a queer philosophy group. He is patient and caring, but feels increasingly hurt by being kept entirely separate from Faisal's family life, while providing the only space where Faisal feels fully seen.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: A homemaker who worries constantly about Faisal's distractedness and weight loss, putting it down to academic stress. She is warm and emotionally intuitive, which makes Faisal's deception feel especially burdensome, as she often asks gentle, perceptive questions he deflects.

npcs.name: Dad
npcs.bio: A minicab driver who works nights and takes pride in providing. He frequently brings up marriage to the daughters of family friends, framing it as a matter of duty, which triggers Faisal's worst anxiety spirals.

npcs.name: Priya
npcs.bio: A coursemate from SOAS who came out as bi in their second year and now lives in a noisy flatshare in Hackney. She was the first person Faisal came out to and remains his most loyal confidante, often reminding him there is no deadline for figuring it all out.

npcs.name: Hugh Brooke
npcs.bio: Eleanor's husband of thirty years, a steady but emotionally distant solicitor. Their marriage has become a quiet arrangement of logistics, and Eleanor secretly questions whether she ever truly loved him.

npcs.name: Oliver Brooke
npcs.bio: Eleanor's youngest, who left for Edinburgh University last September. He rings weekly full of stories, unaware that his mother hides her depression behind a cheerful voice.

npcs.name: Janet Miller
npcs.bio: The head librarian at Richmond Lending Library, who has known Eleanor for over a decade. She's begun checking in more often, and Eleanor feels both comforted and exposed by her concern.

npcs.name: Arthur Clarke
npcs.bio: Eleanor's father, now in a Dorset care home with advanced dementia. Her infrequent visits are heartbreaking, and his slow decline is a quiet, constant grief.

npcs.name: Maya
npcs.bio: Maya is a secondary school art teacher who shares a Brixton flat with Ben. She's increasingly worried as Ben withdraws, unaware he's stopped his medication, and her concern is curdling into quiet resentment.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: Ben's mum lives in Croydon and rings twice a week. She's caring but has a tendency to fuss, which Ben finds smothering when he's low, so he screens her calls more often than not.

npcs.name: Jamal
npcs.bio: Jamal is a fellow session musician and Ben's closest mate in London. He's been covering for Ben's lateness at the Peckham studio but is starting to lose patience.

npcs.name: Ruth
npcs.bio: Ruth runs the recording studio in Peckham and has already cut Ben's hours. She's fair but business-minded, and can't afford an unreliable engineer much longer.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: Aisha's Nigerian mother, a retired nurse, lives in Milton Keynes. She rings every Sunday, fretting over Aisha's health and subtly implying the panic attacks are a spiritual matter that prayer, not therapy, will solve.

npcs.name: Chloe
npcs.bio: Aisha's best friend from university, now a primary school teacher in Walthamstow. Chloe is fiercely protective, but tends to downplay Aisha's corporate struggles with unhelpful 'just leave' advice, not grasping the financial and career stakes.

npcs.name: Mark
npcs.bio: The managing partner supervising Aisha's track. He is outwardly supportive, praising her billable hours, yet has twice spoken over her in client dinners and once suggested she might be 'a bit tense,' missing the structural pressures entirely.

npcs.name: Tunde
npcs.bio: A newly qualified Ghanaian-British solicitor Aisha is meant to mentor. He looks up to her, which adds to her performance anxiety, but their shared experience as Black lawyers in the firm provides a rare space where she doesn't have to translate herself.

npcs.name: Savitri
npcs.bio: Sandeep’s mother in Ahmedabad, who calls daily to check on the family and expects traditional harmony. She frequently reminds Sandeep of his duty to preserve the family’s reputation.

npcs.name: Meera
npcs.bio: Anjali’s widowed mother, living alone in Ahmedabad, who relies on daily video calls for company. She often asks subtle questions about the marriage, adding to Anjali’s sense of being watched.

npcs.name: Nisha Kapoor
npcs.bio: Anjali’s colleague and close friend at the pharmacy, a divorced woman who champions self-care. She is the one person Anjali confides in about the lack of intimacy.

npcs.name: Dr. James Henderson
npcs.bio: The senior GP partner at Sandeep’s surgery, who referred the couple for counselling after noticing Sandeep’s increasing irritability. He is supportive but keeps a professional distance.

npcs.name: Helen Davies
npcs.bio: Helen is a single parent working as a teaching assistant at a local primary school. She loves Charlie but is stretched thin by long hours and money worries, and often misgenders them, leading to frequent arguments.

npcs.name: Riley Okonkwo
npcs.bio: Riley has been Charlie's friend since year 7 and is one of the few who consistently uses they/them pronouns. They've noticed Charlie withdrawing lately but feel helpless to break through the distance.

npcs.name: Alex
npcs.bio: Alex is a non-binary teen from Manchester whom Charlie met on a Discord server. They share late-night chats and memes, but the friendship remains entirely online and sometimes feels unreal.

npcs.name: Miss Thompson
npcs.bio: Miss Thompson teaches A-level Art and recognises Charlie's talent, pushing them to complete coursework. Her well-intentioned pressure only adds to Charlie's guilt and anxiety, as they struggle to find meaning in their work.

npcs.name: Charlotte
npcs.bio: James's wife of eighteen years, a part-time solicitor who manages the household and children's schedules with quiet efficiency. Their dynamic has become a polite but distant co-management of family life, with Charlotte increasingly resentful of his emotional absence and evening drinking.

npcs.name: Dad
npcs.bio: Retired consultant cardiologist living in East Sussex, who embodies a stiff-upper-lip, emotionally reserved paternal style. James feels he is perpetually failing to measure up to a man who never once acknowledged his own struggles.

npcs.name: Eleanor
npcs.bio: James's medical secretary at the hospital, a perceptive and loyal woman in her fifties who has worked with him for over a decade. She gently confronted him about his temper with the junior doctor, prompting his referral, and acts as an informal guardian of his professional reputation.

npcs.name: Tom
npcs.bio: His fourteen-year-old son, a quiet, academically able boy at St Paul's School who has grown used to his father's absence. James is acutely aware that Tom is beginning to mirror his own teenage detachment, and their interactions are reduced to stilted exchanges about school results.

npcs.name: Will
npcs.bio: Will is Naomi's partner and a secondary-school English teacher. He's kind and tries to help, but his long hours and evening commitments mean he often misses the worst of Naomi's struggles, which strains their connection.

npcs.name: Mum
npcs.bio: Naomi's mother lives in Cornwall and they speak briefly on the phone, but the distance—both geographical and emotional—leaves Naomi feeling unable to truly share her pain.

npcs.name: Sarah from baby massage
npcs.bio: Sarah is a fellow new mum Naomi met at the local baby massage class. They chat easily about weaning and sleep regressions, but Naomi holds back her darker feelings for fear of judgement.

npcs.name: Elena (ex-colleague)
npcs.bio: Elena is a former colleague from the Museum of London who has two older children. She checks in occasionally, but her breezy 'you'll be fine' attitude about returning to work often makes Naomi feel more isolated.

npcs.name: Mum (Patricia)
npcs.bio: Retired nurse in Croydon, constantly frets over Paddy's 'lack of direction' and compares him to his more settled sister. Phone calls are a weekly minefield of passive-aggressive concern.

npcs.name: Jamal
npcs.bio: Childhood mate from Peckham, now a youth worker. Always ready with a cuppa and a non-judgemental ear, but gently pushes Paddy to get out of his flat when the low moods hit.

npcs.name: Claire
npcs.bio: Split two years ago after a tense flat-share in Hackney. They still awkwardly orbit the same pub quiz team, and unresolved guilt over how it ended bubbles up whenever Paddy’s anxious.

npcs.name: Nigel
npcs.bio: Line manager at the Southwark call centre, perpetually 'disappointed' by targets. His brusque emails about productivity send Paddy’s Sunday-night dread through the roof.

npcs.name: Mamá
npcs.bio: Carmen, 72, lives alone in a small flat in Sevilla. She worked as a seamstress and still believes Rosa is 'making it' in London. Rosa performs 'todo bien' on their weekly video calls, terrified of disappointing her.

npcs.name: Alejandro
npcs.bio: Rosa's 15-year-old son, in Year 10 at a local academy. He's started picking up shifts at a chicken shop to help out, which Rosa worries is affecting his GCSEs. They argue about money and his future, but he's fiercely protective of his mum.

npcs.name: Tanya from the block
npcs.bio: Lives two floors down in the same tower block. Tanya is a no-nonsense dinner lady who shares surplus food from school and once quietly pushed a £20 note through Rosa's door. They chat in the lift but Rosa still feels she can't fully confide.

npcs.name: Derek, line manager
npcs.bio: Manages the domestic services team at King's College Hospital. A decent man under pressure, he calls Rosa for extra shifts at short notice. He knows she's struggling but the admin system is inflexible, leaving Rosa feeling like a 'pair of hands' rather than a person.

npcs.name: Camille
npcs.bio: A warm and perceptive graphic designer Lucas met at an architecture exhibition six months ago. She senses his guardedness and is gently trying to build intimacy, but grows anxious and frustrated by his unexplained emotional withdrawals and the barrier she feels.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: A retired school secretary living in Tours, who is fiercely devoted to Lucas. Her frequent, anxious check-ins, while loving, feel suffocating to Lucas, as she sees his struggle as a sign he needs to move back home, which he resists.

npcs.name: Hugo's mum, Sylvie
npcs.bio: The mother of Lucas's best friend Hugo, who died at the Bataclan. Since the attack, she has maintained a painfully polite but extremely distant connection, sending a card on the anniversary but unable to engage; her unresolved grief and silent blame are a constant ghost in Lucas's mind.

npcs.name: Mateo from work
npcs.bio: A pragmatic and supportive senior project manager at the architecture agency. He covers for Lucas's recent errors without drawing attention to it, encouraging him to take his time, but his stoic kindness makes Lucas feel even more of an impostor.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Widowed five years ago and now living alone in the family flat in Montreuil. She phones Aïcha daily, fretting about her well-being while simultaneously leaning on her for emotional and logistical support.

npcs.name: Léa
npcs.bio: Aïcha's ten-year-old daughter, bright and sensitive. She has started acting out at school since the separation, and Aïcha worries endlessly about the impact on her.

npcs.name: Ibrahim
npcs.bio: Younger brother who works in IT and lives nearby in Bagnolet. He is practical and calm, often stepping in to help with Léa or household repairs, but he can be dismissive of Aïcha's anxiety.

npcs.name: Sarah from work
npcs.bio: A friendly peer at the small accounting firm in the 11th arrondissement. She covers for Aïcha when she needs to leave early for Léa, but has recently hinted she feels taken advantage of.

npcs.name: Catherine Dumont
npcs.bio: A juge d'instruction at the Tribunal de Paris, Catherine is a high-achiever who expects control. She has grown weary of Pierre's decline and issued an ultimatum, yet still hopes therapy will restore their former partnership.

npcs.name: Léa Dumont
npcs.bio: Studying medicine at Université Paris Cité, Léa is absorbed in her own pressures but worries about her father during weekend visits. Her future and the cost of her education weigh heavily on Pierre's mind.

npcs.name: François Moreau
npcs.bio: Pierre's direct superior at the Direction générale du Trésor, François is a demanding technocrat whose exacting standards exacerbate Pierre's fear of exposure. Catherine's threat to inform him about Pierre's state looms large.

npcs.name: Marc Lemoine
npcs.bio: A younger, ambitious colleague at the Trésor, Marc's rapid rise and competence highlight Pierre's own sense of inadequacy, creating a silent rivalry that fuels Pierre's self-doubt.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Sofia's mother is a répétiteur at the Opéra and a Lacanian psychoanalyst who has always interpreted Sofia's every action as a signifier. Their dynamic is one of psychological control, leaving Sofia feeling never truly seen.

npcs.name: Papa
npcs.bio: Sofia's father lives in Bologna, a retired literature professor who left the family when she was twelve. He is kind but emotionally distant, offering occasional phone calls that never address her eating.

npcs.name: Chloé
npcs.bio: Chloé is a fellow corps dancer a year younger, warm-hearted but also fiercely competitive. She tries to support Sofia, yet their conversations often circle back to weight and casting, unintentionally fuelling Sofia's anxiety.

npcs.name: Dr Lefèvre
npcs.bio: Dr Lefèvre is the Opéra's médecin du travail, a calm and observant man who noticed Sofia's decline. He made the referral with genuine concern but remains a peripheral figure in her daily life.

npcs.name: Aïssatou Sow
npcs.bio: Mamadou's wife, living in Dakar with their two young children. She relies on his irregular remittances and grows increasingly frustrated and suspicious, though she does not know the full extent of his addiction.

npcs.name: Camille Dufour
npcs.bio: The Aurore association outreach worker who referred Mamadou to the CSAPA. She helps him navigate benefits and appointments, but her professional distance sometimes feels like a barrier to deeper trust.

npcs.name: Ibrahim Diallo
npcs.bio: A fellow migrant from Mali who shares a room in the foyer. He and Mamadou often use crack together, but Ibrahim has recently expressed a desire to stop, causing friction and mutual temptation.

npcs.name: Antoine Moreau
npcs.bio: A former co-worker from the construction site who saw Mamadou's accident. He visits sporadically out of guilt, bringing painful reminders of the trauma and the life Mamadou lost.

npcs.name: Claire Roux
npcs.bio: A retired literature professor and staunch secularist who interprets Camille's conversion as a rejection of her upbringing; their rare phone calls are laced with passive-aggressive remarks about 'irrationality'.

npcs.name: Philippe Roux
npcs.bio: A mild-mannered architect who avoids conflict, he maintains a distant but affectionate email correspondence with Camille, sharing articles on art and architecture without ever addressing the family rift.

npcs.name: Luc Roux
npcs.bio: Her younger brother, a pragmatic engineer based in Lyon, who loves Camille but finds her religious fervour baffling; he calls weekly and gently encourages her to see a psychiatrist, worried about her isolation.

npcs.name: Antoine Girard
npcs.bio: Camille's editor at Le Monde, he admires her writing but is under pressure from his own superiors; he sends increasingly terse emails about missed deadlines, unaware of the rituals that delay her work.

npcs.name: Antoine
npcs.bio: Émilie's husband, a 41-year-old finance manager working long hours in La Défense. He provides financially but is physically absent, leaving before 7:30 and returning near 22:00. He knows only an edited version of her struggles and believes the sertraline will fix things.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Émilie's mother, based in Lyon. Offers regular video calls filled with well-meaning but unhelpful advice and gentle criticism about bottle-feeding. She represents a traditional standard of motherhood Émilie feels she has failed.

npcs.name: Chloé from work
npcs.bio: A fellow associate and Émilie's closest friend in Paris, now handling her caseload during maternity leave. They used to share commiserating drinks after long hours. Chloé sends cheerful but clueless texts about 'enjoying the break', which deepens Émilie's isolation.

npcs.name: Dr. Morel
npcs.bio: The compassionate PMI doctor who spotted the warning signs at Sébastien's 5-month check and gently encouraged Émilie to seek help. She prescribed the initial sertraline and referred her to a specialist. Émilie feels both grateful and exposed.

npcs.name: Yasmine
npcs.bio: Karim's wife of 18 years, a meticulous dentist who manages the family's accounts—and discovered his escort spending. Now icily polite, she communicates only logistics from behind a wall of hurt, her trust shattered.

npcs.name: Sami
npcs.bio: Their 16-year-old son, bright and increasingly withdrawn, who has sensed the marital fracture. He mirrors Karim's own adolescent disappointment, his silent judgments landing like a verdict Karim has dreaded since boyhood.

npcs.name: Nabil
npcs.bio: Karim's sous-chef and oldest friend from the neighbourhood, who knows the restaurant books well enough to suspect something was off. He hasn't asked directly but has started covering shifts without question, a quiet, steady presence.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Karim's widowed mother, now in a retirement flat in the 19e, who still speaks of his late father's charm with a mix of bitterness and longing. She relies on Karim for weekly visits and financial help, never suspecting how closely he has followed the paternal script.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: A Lacanian psychoanalyst practising on Rue Bonaparte who incessantly interprets Élise's behaviour as text. Her clinical curiosity replaces maternal warmth, leaving Élise feeling like a case study rather than a daughter.

npcs.name: Papa
npcs.bio: Political philosophy professor at Sciences Po who turns every conversation into an intellectual debate. He deflects emotional concerns with abstract concepts, failing to see the fragility beneath Élise's composed surface.

npcs.name: Clémence
npcs.bio: A calm and unpretentious childhood friend who has known Élise since primary school. She offers quiet companionship and distraction without probing, but is increasingly shut out by Élise's secretive rituals.

npcs.name: Mr Keller
npcs.bio: Her philosophy teacher at Lycée Henri-IV, who has mentored her toward the concours général. He lavishes praise on her intellect while remaining oblivious to her physical decline, adding pressure to excel.

npcs.name: Théo Marchand
npcs.bio: A 41-year-old architect Manon met at a talk on urban commons. He is confident, emotionally open, and unaware of the couple's crisis, simply enjoying a deepening connection with Manon. His presence has become the catalyst for rupture.

npcs.name: Lucie Moreau
npcs.bio: A close university friend of both Antoine and Manon, now a librarian in the 11th arrondissement. She has known them since before the PACS and provides a calm, non-judgemental ear, often hosting them separately for dinner and listening.

npcs.name: Jean Girard
npcs.bio: Antoine's retired father living in Lyon, who has always been uneasy with his son's freelance career and unconventional relationship. He phones weekly, offering unsolicited advice about financial security and 'settling down', adding a layer of pressure.

npcs.name: Camille Lefèvre
npcs.bio: Manon's older sister, a primary-school teacher in Nantes. She is supportive of Manon's emotional honesty but privately worries that the situation with Théo will end painfully, and her cautious questions sometimes unsettle Manon.

npcs.name: Édouard
npcs.bio: Nina's fiancé, a thoughtful junior magistrate at the Tribunal de Paris. He is deeply concerned by her panic attacks but expresses it through practical problem-solving—researching alternative commutes and gently suggesting she 'just try' the métro again, which inadvertently adds pressure.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Nina's mother, a stoic first-generation immigrant who runs a textile shop in Belleville. She rarely speaks of emotions but conveys expectation through loaded silences and comments about the upcoming wedding; her pride in Nina is immense, yet it feels like a debt.

npcs.name: Linh
npcs.bio: Nina's older sister, who left Paris for Marseille with her husband. Viewed by the family as the rebellious one, Linh is actually a warm and perceptive confidante who, during rare phone calls, gently questions if Nina is truly happy, providing a lifeline of unspoken understanding.

npcs.name: Sabine from the pharmacie
npcs.bio: A chatty, well-meaning préparatrice en pharmacie who has worked with Nina for two years. She notices Nina's exhaustion and covers for her lateness without comment, but her constant stream of neighbourhood gossip can feel overwhelming to Nina during a busy shift.

npcs.name: Frédéric
npcs.bio: Jean-Paul's late partner of 30 years, a photographer who documented their life together. He died two years ago from pancreatic cancer, and Jean-Paul has kept their flat exactly as he left it.

npcs.name: Camille
npcs.bio: Frédéric's niece from Lyon, who handles the administrative remnants of the estate. Their interactions are polite but strained, as she represents a future without Frédéric that Jean-Paul resists.

npcs.name: Lucas
npcs.bio: A younger gay artist in his thirties who befriended Jean-Paul after a community event. He treats Jean-Paul with a reverence that feels alienating, seeing him as a survivor icon rather than a person.

npcs.name: Alain
npcs.bio: An old friend from the ACT UP Paris days, also living with HIV. They share a bond of having outlived many friends, but their meetings are tinged with survivor's guilt and unspoken grief.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Yana's mother, who stayed behind in Mariupol and died during the siege. There was no funeral or body to bury, leaving Yana with crushing guilt and unresolved grief that surfaces in daily life.

npcs.name: Antoine
npcs.bio: Yana's wealthy employer from the 16e arrondissement, who hires her via CESU for exhausting, irregular cleaning hours. He is demanding and the financial dependence adds pressure.

npcs.name: Olena
npcs.bio: A fellow Ukrainian refugee in Boulogne-Billancourt who helps with childcare and shares meals. Her presence is a rare source of emotional comfort and cultural connection.

npcs.name: Dr. Lévy
npcs.bio: The PMI psychologist who noticed Yana's distress at a school meeting and gently but persistently encouraged her to start trauma therapy. Their previous brief contact left Yana both grateful and wary.

npcs.name: Sylvie
npcs.bio: Sylvie works for the local council and has been holding the household together. She is exhausted and has told Marc she no longer recognises him, but she desperately wants him to get help.

npcs.name: Julien
npcs.bio: Julien, the eldest, works in IT in Lyon. He worries about his father and calls regularly, offering practical help, but Marc often brushes him off, feeling ashamed.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Marc's mother has been in a care home near Sarcelles for three years, increasingly frail and forgetful. His dutiful visits leave him hollow and add to his guilt.

npcs.name: Thierry
npcs.bio: Thierry is a fellow train driver who joined SNCF with Marc thirty years ago. He still texts Marc about depot life, but his messages now feel like a reproach rather than a lifeline.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Léa's mother, living in Marseille, who cannot accept Léa's decision not to have children, resulting in frequent arguments and a strained, increasingly distant relationship.

npcs.name: Chloé
npcs.bio: Fellow normalienne and flatmate in the rue d'Ulm residence, who gently tries to support Léa but often feels shut out by her anxious withdrawal.

npcs.name: Prof. Lefèvre
npcs.bio: Distinguished philosopher supervising Léa's mémoire; provides intellectually stimulating guidance but his high standards inadvertently fuel her perfectionism and eco-anxiety.

npcs.name: Antoine
npcs.bio: Léa's younger brother, still in Marseille, who cares for her but feels caught in the middle of the family conflict, offering sporadic support.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Aïcha, 72, has late-stage Alzheimer’s and moved in with Faiza after a fall six months ago. She needs constant supervision, and on rare lucid nights she asks Faiza why she is so tired, which both comforts and devastates her daughter.

npcs.name: Rachid
npcs.bio: Rachid, 44, works long hours at Rungis wholesale market, leaving home before dawn. He loves Faiza deeply but is worn down himself and struggles to see how close she is to breaking. He tries to help with the children on weekends but often retreats into the TV, and their intimacy has faded into exhaustion and unspoken disappointment.

npcs.name: Inès
npcs.bio: Inès, 15, has become the de facto second parent, helping with her younger siblings and grandmother while Faiza works. She is responsible and loving but increasingly resentful, skipping schoolwork and snapping at her mother that she ‘didn’t ask for this’ – which fills Faiza with guilt that she is stealing her daughter’s youth.

npcs.name: Leïla
npcs.bio: Leïla, 38, lives in Créteil with her husband and two young children. She has always been Faiza’s confidante, but since their mother moved in, Faiza has stopped calling. Leïla feels shut out and frustrated, occasionally sending sharp texts about Faiza's ‘martyr complex,’ which Faiza deletes without replying – deepening the rift.

npcs.name: Amélie
npcs.bio: Olivier's ex-wife, a museum curator who now lives in Saint-Germain-en-Laye with their three children. She is pushing for supervised visitation after the children reported his volatile moods, and communication between them is now entirely via avocats.

npcs.name: Luc
npcs.bio: Olivier's 12-year-old son, bright and observant, who has become increasingly withdrawn during visits. Olivier senses Luc is beginning to see him through his mother's eyes, which triggers a deep, unspoken terror of repeating his own father's legacy.

npcs.name: Jean-Marc from the desk
npcs.bio: A junior trader on Olivier's fixed-income desk who normalises the cocaine use as part of 'desk culture'. He is a drinking-and-using buddy who enables Olivier's denial by treating the habit as unremarkable professional lubrication.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Olivier's widowed mother, now living in a retirement residence in Versailles. She calls him weekly, speaking in gentle, worried tones about his health and the divorce, but remains emotionally fragile and leans on him for reassurance, reinforcing his belief that he must be the strong one.

npcs.name: Amina (flatmate)
npcs.bio: Amina is a poetic, quietly perceptive French-Tunisian activist and Inès’s closest flatmate. She senses Inès is struggling but often holds back, fearing she’ll overstep or revive old wounds.

npcs.name: Uncle Karim
npcs.bio: Karim, a retired printer living in Asnières, provided Inès’s first stable home in France before severing contact after she began hormone therapy. Inès still sends him WhatsApp messages that go unanswered.

npcs.name: Jérôme, salon manager
npcs.bio: Jérôme runs the 11e arrondissement salon where Inès is an apprentice. He enjoys her quiet diligence but is unaware of how close she came to being sacked after a dissociative episode at work.

npcs.name: Sarah from planning familial
npcs.bio: Sarah is the pragmatic GP at the local planning familial clinic who has shepherded Inès through HRT and referred her for therapy. She remains a steady, non-intrusive anchor point.

npcs.name: Aurélie
npcs.bio: Henri's wife of 14 years, a sommelière with a sharp palate and a busy schedule. She has noticed the late-night kitchen raids and bathroom visits but has never addressed them, creating a heavy silence between them. She loves Henri but feels increasingly isolated and unsure how to help.

npcs.name: Thierry Morin
npcs.bio: The owner-chef of the bistronomique restaurant, a demanding perfectionist who treats Henri more like a machine than a person. He piles on responsibilities without acknowledgement, and his frequent criticisms in front of the brigade feed Henri's sense of never being good enough.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Henri's elderly mother, now residing in a retirement home in the banlieue after a mild stroke. Emotionally reserved throughout his childhood, she still shows affection only through criticism of his life choices. Her recent health issues have stirred up guilt and a sense of duty in Henri.

npcs.name: Antoine
npcs.bio: A childhood friend from the same banlieue estate, now running a small neighbourhood bistro in Montreuil. They meet fortnightly for a beer, and Antoine provides unpretentious camaraderie. However, Henri has never confided his eating disorder, maintaining a facade of everything being 'fine'.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Carmen's elderly mother lives alone in Seville, increasingly frail and hard of hearing. Since Patrick's death, Carmen has resumed weekly phone calls, but the conversations are strained by unspoken guilt on Carmen's side and gentle, anxious questioning on her mother's.

npcs.name: Anaïs
npcs.bio: Carmen's daughter is a bright, politically engaged master's student in Lyon. She calls twice a week and is openly worried, pushing Carmen to see a therapist and offering practical support, but her own grief makes her occasionally impatient with her mother's inertia.

npcs.name: Sandrine from the canteen
npcs.bio: A fellow canteen worker who has known Carmen for a decade. She covers for Carmen's moments of distraction, often silently leaving a coffee on her tray without a fuss. She is stolid, undemanding and represents the possibility of low-key, non-judgemental human contact.

npcs.name: Théo
npcs.bio: Carmen's son works as an engineer in Bordeaux and is emotionally reserved. He calls fortnightly and focuses on practical solutions, recently suggesting Carmen downsize or move closer to him, a proposal that makes Carmen feel managed rather than comforted.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: A high-powered corporate lawyer who monitors BFM TV constantly. She believes Tristan needs medication and strict discipline, and weeps when he disrupts family dinners.

npcs.name: Garance
npcs.bio: Tristan's fifteen-year-old sister, an ambitious lycéenne aiming for Sciences Po. She is the only family member who appreciates his wit, privately calling him 'amusant'.

npcs.name: Théo
npcs.bio: A classmate at the bilingual collège who enjoys Tristan's clever disruptions but sometimes gets labelled as trouble by association. They bond over shared mischief during breaks.

npcs.name: M. Lefèvre
npcs.bio: The headteacher of the private collège who recently called the parents to report Tristan's 'unmanageable' behaviour. His ultimatums escalate the parental blame game.

npcs.name: Olivier
npcs.bio: Aurélie's partner of two years and direct superior at an LVMH fashion house. He is a reserved, pragmatic man who cares for her but has grown weary of the emotional intensity, recently describing her as 'exhausting' after a minor deception.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Retired and living in a quiet suburb of Lyon, she is a steady, undemonstrative presence who sends care packages but struggles to understand Aurélie's inner world, often defaulting to practical advice that feels dismissive.

npcs.name: Chloé from work
npcs.bio: A junior publicist on Aurélie's team who admires her talent but walks on eggshells, having witnessed a dramatic stairwell argument with Olivier. She is friendly but keeps a careful distance to protect her own position.

npcs.name: Dr Benoît
npcs.bio: The psychiatrist who led Aurélie's DBT group at Sainte-Anne years ago. She still occasionally emails him in moments of crisis, and his brief, kind replies are a lifeline, though she fears she has disappointed him by not 'graduating' from her patterns.

npcs.name: Ladan
npcs.bio: Reza's wife, living in Toronto with their son Amin and her family. She manages a dual burden of maintaining hope for reunification while coping with the daily reality of raising a child alone, which has worn down her patience and created a strained, anxious dynamic with Reza.

npcs.name: Mehdi
npcs.bio: An Iranian acquaintance from the Parisian diaspora whom Reza avoids when unwell. They share a history of cautious solidarity, but their contact is infrequent and governed by unspoken rules about discussing their precarious situations, making him a peripheral but potential lifeline.

npcs.name: Dr. Laurent
npcs.bio: Reza's psychiatrist at the CMP du 12e, who has overseen his care since discharge. Their relationship is based on clinical trust and Reza's meticulous compliance, but the doctor's purely medical framing inadvertently reinforces Reza's tendency to pathologise all his fears.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Reza's mother, still in Tehran. Their phone calls are cherished but filled with unspoken grief over the family's dispersal and her own fragile health, making contact a source of comfort shadowed by guilt and dread of the call that brings bad news.

npcs.name: Clémence
npcs.bio: The Roberts' youngest, now a first-year at Sciences Po. She's picked up on the strained atmosphere at home and has pulled away, cancelling Sunday dinners and being vague about her life. Sandrine feels she's losing her daughter too.

npcs.name: Sophie
npcs.bio: A friend from Sandrine's pilates class who discreetly passed on the therapist's details. She listens sympathetically but sometimes fuels Sandrine's resentment by echoing her complaints about Philippe.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Philippe's elderly mother, recently diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's, lives alone in Lyon. She needs increasing assistance, and Philippe feels guilty for not visiting more, adding to his emotional withdrawal at home.

npcs.name: Isabelle
npcs.bio: Sandrine's directrice at TotalEnergies, who is pushing her team through another round of restructuring with exacting expectations. The long hours and moral fatigue leave Sandrine with little patience for therapy homework.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: She believes Zineb's increased washing is a sign of heightened devotion and often praises her for it, unaware of the distress it causes. She worries about Zineb's exhaustion but attributes it to academic stress.

npcs.name: Papa
npcs.bio: A retired municipal worker, he is proud of Zineb's education but frequently reminds her of the family's financial sacrifices. He interprets her rituals as normal religious practice and focuses primarily on her academic performance.

npcs.name: Amina
npcs.bio: Zineb's 18-year-old sister who looks up to her. Amina has begun to notice something is wrong and has tried to talk about the hand washing, but Zineb deflects. She feels shut out and is unsure how to help.

npcs.name: Imam Rashid
npcs.bio: The imam of the mosque Zineb used to attend; he is kind and knowledgeable about religious scrupulosity, but Zineb fears he will confirm her worst fears about her faith, so she avoids him. He has inquired about her well-being through others.

npcs.name: Gérard Renault
npcs.bio: Gérard is a retired magistrate who has retreated into his study of Napoleonic law. He loves Frédérique deeply but no longer knows how to reach her, and their meals have become silent, parallel routines.

npcs.name: Dr. Karim Khalil
npcs.bio: Dr. Khalil is a kind, observant GP who gently insisted Frédérique seek therapy after noticing her weight loss and insomnia. He remains a steady, concerned presence, checking in during routine appointments.

npcs.name: Chantal Moreau
npcs.bio: Chantal is a diplomat's wife and a long-time friend from the days of embassy dinners. She has tried repeatedly to invite Frédérique for tea, but her chatter about grandchildren inadvertently deepens Frédérique's isolation.

npcs.name: Dr. Hélène Lefèvre
npcs.bio: Dr. Lefèvre is a pragmatic psychiatrist who recommended medication for Frédérique's grief, which she refused. The therapeutic relationship ended with Frédérique feeling pathologised and misunderstood.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: An architect who discovered Mathilde's self-harm and arranged private therapy; she hovers anxiously, trying to monitor her daughter's wellbeing, which Mathilde finds both caring and suffocating.

npcs.name: Antoine
npcs.bio: A philosopher and columnist who writes publicly about supporting LGBT youth, but Mathilde experiences his backing as a distant performance rather than genuine fatherly presence.

npcs.name: Chloé
npcs.bio: Mathilde's former closest friend and brief romantic interest; after Mathilde confessed her feelings, Chloé withdrew abruptly, leaving Mathilde isolated and hurt.

npcs.name: Catherine
npcs.bio: Mathilde's empathetic literature teacher at Lycée Voltaire, who has noticed her slumping grades and offers extra support, though Mathilde remains guarded.

npcs.name: Maman
npcs.bio: Retired pharmacist in Lyon who communicates mostly through practical texts about meals and weather. Since Sylvain told her about the patient's death, she has sent a single message saying 'Il faut du temps' and has not called, leaving Sylvain feeling emotionally abandoned.

npcs.name: Papa
npcs.bio: Retired GP who frames all distress within a medical model of resilience. He told Sylvain not to make a 'personal drama' of the suicide, deepening Sylvain's sense that his grief is illegitimate and must be hidden.

npcs.name: Dr. Benoît
npcs.bio: A senior registrar on the same unit who has started leaving coffee on Sylvain's desk without comment. They rarely speak, but Benoît is the only person who has not avoided Sylvain since Léo's death.

npcs.name: Lise
npcs.bio: Fellow psychiatry resident with whom Sylvain shared a flat until their relationship ended a year ago. They still exchange occasional texts about conference papers, but Sylvain has not told her about Léo, fearing her clinical judgement.
